data.title: Lichen spinulosus — viva
data.summary: Disorders of keratinisation · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Lichen spinulosus** (Disorders of keratinisation)_

**Q1. What is lichen spinulosus?**
- Uncommon follicular keratotic eruption, mainly in children and adolescents (boys), with grouped skin-coloured follicular papules each bearing a filiform keratin spine, arranged in round/oval plaques 2–6 cm on neck, buttocks, abdomen, extensor limbs, trunk; feels like a nutmeg grater

**Q2. Aetiology / associations.**
- Mostly idiopathic; atopy, vitamin A deficiency (overlap with phrynoderma), seborrhoeic dermatitis; reported in HIV (with PRP type VI), Crohn's disease, alcoholism, drugs (gold, thallium), lymphoma, syphilis, fungal (id)

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Dilated follicular infundibula filled with keratin plugs (spinous projections above the surface), sparse perifollicular lymphocytes

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Keratosis pilaris (diffuse, not grouped plaques), phrynoderma (malnutrition, larger papules on elbows/knees), PRP (follicular papules on knuckles, orange keratoderma), lichen nitidus (shiny, flat, not spiny), lichen scrofulosorum (TB — yellow-brown lichenoid grouped papules; Mantoux positive), trichodysplasia spinulosa (polyomavirus in immunosuppressed — face), multiple minute digitate hyperkeratoses, follicular eczema, Darier's disease

**Q5. Treatment.**
- Often asymptomatic and self-limiting (months to years)
- Keratolytics: urea 10–20%, salicylic acid 3–6%, lactic acid 12%; topical retinoids; mild topical steroids
- Correct nutritional deficiencies (vitamin A); treat underlying cause (HIV etc.)

**Q6. Describe the clinical features.**
- Children/adolescents (boys more): grouped skin-coloured to slightly red follicular papules each topped by a fine horny spine, forming well-defined round plaques 2–6 cm on neck, trunk, extensor limbs, buttocks; feel like a nutmeg grater; asymptomatic or mildly itchy; symmetrical

**Q7. Name the associations.**
- Atopy, seborrhoeic dermatitis; also reported with HIV, Hodgkin lymphoma, alcoholism, Crohn's disease, vitamin A deficiency (phrynoderma-like), drugs (gold, thallium); 'generalised lichen spinulosus' in adults should prompt systemic evaluation

**Q8. Which other disorders produce follicular spiny papules?**
- Keratosis pilaris, phrynoderma, PRP, Darier's disease, lichen planopilaris, follicular eczema, trichodysplasia spinulosa (polyomavirus in immunosuppressed), multiple minute digitate hyperkeratoses, spiny keratoderma, myeloma-associated follicular spicules

**Q9. Prognosis?**
- Self-limiting — often resolves by puberty; recurrences possible; keratolytics speed improvement

## Quick spotter facts
- Grouped spiny follicular papules forming a plaque on the neck of a child — lichen spinulosus
- Differentiate from lichen scrofulosorum (TB)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Follicular keratoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
